A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SE-RL/SP-RL study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original action-aliasing experiments and TD3/A2C evaluations on pendulum, quadrotor, and seeker tasks, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds energy-management results, penalty-critic learning diagnostics, and measured runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: The projection procedure, SE-RL/SP-RL formulations, per-sample loss, and proposed penalty critic remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 newly documents the penalty critic's architecture and training target without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds an energy-management task controlling a battery and heat pump using forecasts, with competing electricity-cost and temperature objectives (Appendix A.8.4). This substantially broadens coverage beyond the retained stabilization and navigation tasks.

E2.justification: Both versions compare vanilla SE-RL, SE-RL Penalty, vanilla SP-RL, SP-RL PSL, and SP-RL PenC using TD3 and A2C. The added energy-management evaluations use the same comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces runtime measurement over 10,000 TD3 steps normalized to vanilla SE-RL, and an EMS protocol with five forecasts and randomized one-day episodes. Seeker dynamics also change from the disturbance-free equation in v1 to explicitly include bounded uniform disturbances in v2; this reported setting revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8 and Appendix A.7 add direct analysis of penalty-weight effects on critic-loss stability and safeguard interventions across four tasks. Appendix A.9 adds a controlled computational-cost comparison where v1 explicitly omitted detailed wall-clock analysis. These substantially extend the existing return-based sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seven training runs evaluated on ten random seeds, interquartile means with 95% bootstrap intervals, appendix means and standard deviations, and Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn tests with Bonferroni correction. No new statistical estimation procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the six original benchmark tables are retained. v2 adds EMS results, critic-loss trajectories, and runtime ratios. For example, Table 6 reports TD3 EMS returns of -12.59 +/- 5.13 for PenC at w=2 versus -26.45 +/- 19.25 for vanilla SP-RL. Table 2 adds SP-RL runtime ratios ranging from 3.55 to 12.51.

T1.justification: v2 removes the projected-mean log-likelihood and gradient derivation from v1 Appendix A.5. Appendix A.1 also changes its noise assumption from bounded Gaussian noise to bounded noise. The central optimal-value and GAE-equivalence results and their proofs remain substantively intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about optimal-value equivalence, stochastic-policy equivalence, differing action-aliasing effects, and the proposed penalty critic. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of EMS objective alignment and penalty-critic stability. Section 9 explains runtime differences through projection complexity and dimensionality and discusses parallel decomposition. Section 6.3 also narrows the stochastic-policy flat-lining statement from both frameworks to SE-RL.

D1.justification: v2 adds an implementation-repository link and a dedicated subsection specifying the penalty critic's separate network, shared architecture specification, squared-error training, and bootstrap target. It also documents EMS observations, dynamics, rewards, constraints, and episode construction, substantially expanding implementation and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: New citations include Boyd and Vandenberghe, Bertsekas, Schervish, Bianchi, and Grontas et al., supporting definitions, proof exposition, the EMS model, and computational discussion. The central positioning against previous SE-RL/SP-RL research is retained; publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language edits, clarifies proof explanations, separates the aliasing and flat-lining statements, and reorganizes targeted appendix subsections. Author/publication information and acknowledgments are updated. The main section sequence and most narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The training and test-result figures exchange numbering and expand from three to four task columns. v2 adds the eight-panel Figure 8 and runtime/EMS Tables 2, 6, and 10, reformats existing result-table headers and rules, and redraws or relocates aliasing illustrations. Table 9 also loses the original first w=0.1 heading.

improvement.justification: Measured runtime comparisons, penalty-critic stability diagnostics, and implementation details provide a practical improvement over v1, which omitted detailed timing. Added EMS coverage is useful but has reporting ambiguities: Table 10 repeats Table 6's entire PSL column and reports unequal A2C penalty-variant results despite the text's equivalence statement. These concerns limit confidence in the new EMS evidence.
